newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds slide in light Monday trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds slide in light Monday trade.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities drifted lower in light trading at late-afternoon, but yield spreads to Treasuries were steady to slightly tighter.
A dearth of economic data contained volatility on Monday and will likely do so for the remainder of the week, traders and analysts said.
"It's just near dead," said one East Coast regional mortgage trader. "(Volatility) is like the Friday after the Thanksgiving holiday," he said.
Many traders left early for the Passover holiday.
By late afternoon, Ginnie Mae 30-year 8.0-percent paper was off 4/32 at 100-26/32 bid, yielding 118 basis points over the five-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae paper fell 7/32 at 100-26/32 bid, and Freddie Mac issues slipped 4/32 at 101-02/32 bid.
Five-year Treasuries were down 5/32 at 6.75 percent, and 10-year notes were off 8/32 at 6.86 percent.
The lack of economic data should keep mortgage-backeds in a tight range, said Cynthia Rivera, mortgage analyst at BZW Securities Inc.
"The fact that we have no economic data is going to continue to cheapen (market) volatility," she said.
Rivera recommended that longer-term investors of pass-throughs should not overweight but stick with their current portfolio weightings.
"In addition, the roll market should offer more viable opportunities for increasing total returns once (Fannie Mae) callable deals begin to get underway," she said.
